_notes: Vanilla brushing, recorded by Obsidian.AssetGenerator/Java/BrushingFixtures.java (CaptureFixtures=brushing) on a headless dedicated server in a flat world of air. The target is suspicious sand or gravel (or another block) at `target`, set without updates with its `lootTable` and `seed` or a `storedItem`. The user stands at `player` (x, y, z, yaw, pitch; the case's own `player` if it has one), with its head and last rotation the same, holding a brush (`damage`, `handUsed`, `gameMode`). Tick 0 clicks the target's `face` through ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn. Each later tick advances the game time, runs the due block ticks, ticks the area's entities, then ticks the user's use of the item (LivingEntity.updatingUsingItem), as a server tick does. `actions` run before their tick's work: look (yaw, pitch), move, release (releaseUsingItem), set (a state at an offset with UPDATE_ALL), select (hotbar slot) and click. The timeline keeps each tick that did something: the click's result, the ordered writes with their flags (from a neighbour updater wrapping the level's: UPDATE_NEIGHBORS from the neighbour update, the rest from the shape updates' flags; null for a change neither saw), the sounds (id, source, offset, volume, pitch), level events and particles a bystander three blocks above received, the entity events of the user's tracked entity (to the bystander and the user), game events within 16 blocks, statistics, advancement criteria completed (`criteria` registers player_generates_container_loot), the used hand's item, whether the user is still using it, the target block entity's saved data when it changed (null once gone), its update tag (`clientData`) when the target's state was written, and the entities that appeared (items with position and motion, falling blocks with their state) or went. Positions are relative to the target. Vanilla aims the brush each tick with ProjectileUtil.getHitResultOnViewVector over collision shapes, from the eyes along the view of the last tick's head rotation.
